result.title: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems
result.summary: Frontier artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly operating over longer horizons with diminishing human oversight, raising the risk of loss of control: systems acting beyond effective human control with potentially irreversible consequences. Because such failures may become observable only after containment is difficult, they must be assessed prospectively. We introduce a behavioural framework that decomposes loss-of-control risk into three factors: misaligned motive, harm-enabling capability, and monitoring evasion. We operationalise these factors through 13 measurable aspects and 29 evaluation tasks, whose scores are combined into a single loss-of-control (LoC) score. Across 13 frontier models, the LoC score shows strong prospective validity, correlating with failure rates in contained long-horizon risk scenarios (Pearson r = 0.84). Risk varies systematically across models and cannot be explained by capability alone. We further show that the framework can guide targeted mitigations: fine-tuning and monitoring directed at diagnosed vulnerabilities reduce failure rates while largely preserving general performance. These results provide a practical basis for predicting, understanding, and mitigating loss-of-control risk before it materialises.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一个行为学框架，把前沿AI系统的「失控」风险拆为动机错位、致害能力与规避监控三因素，经13个方面、29项评测任务合成单一LoC分数，并在13个模型上验证该分数与受控长时程风险场景失败率相关（r=0.84），同时用以指导针对性微调与监控。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无直接关系，但其「规避监控」维度及以下游失败率检验前瞻效度的做法，可能为latent推理状态难以审计、难以监控时的评价与监督设计提供可供核查的概念线索。
